task: Backlog #11 - real avatars on the Messages page, with an initial fallback for users who have no uploaded avatar
working_directory: repository root (~/aws-bootcamp-cruddur-2023). All paths below are relative to it.

context.problem:
The message-group list draws a solid purple circle for every user. MessageGroupItem.js renders an empty
and never uses ProfileAvatar. Even if it did, the data cannot support it: Ddb.list_message_groups returns uuid, display_name, handle, message and created_at, but not cognito_user_id, and ProfileAvatar builds the image URL from cognito_user_id.
context.design_backend: Enrich at read time. services/message_groups.py already has every handle on the page; it makes ONE Postgres query (WHERE users.handle = ANY(%(handles)s)) and attaches cognito_user_id to each group before returning. DynamoDB item shape is NOT changed, so no backfill of existing items is needed. A handle with no matching user gets None.
context.design_frontend: ProfileAvatar gains an optional `name` prop and a fallback: if `id` is missing, or the fires onError (the user never uploaded an avatar, so S3/CloudFront returns 403/404), it renders a purple circle containing the first letter of `name`, or '?' when no name is given. MessageGroupItem renders ProfileAvatar inside its existing 50px circle.
context.blast_radius: ProfileAvatar is shared with the home feed (ActivityContent). For users WITH an avatar the home feed is unchanged: same element, same src, same classes. The only home-feed change is that a broken image becomes a '?' circle. The new CSS is scoped with :has(.avatar-fallback) so it applies ONLY in the fallback case.
context.why_no_sql_comments: db.query_array_json wraps the template inside FROM ( ... ) array_row. A trailing `--` comment line could swallow the closing parenthesis, and a semicolon would break the wrap. The new SQL file therefore has NO comments and NO semicolon, like home.sql.
context.gate_authoring_note: Gates below grep for exact CODE strings with grep -F, chosen so they cannot also match the prose comments this spec mandates. If a gate still returns an unexpected count, report it; do NOT edit comments or content to make a gate pass.
